\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.AverageInfluence}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Average influence]
\lean{FABL.averageInfluence}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p064-b009,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b006
}
\label{FABL.averageInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.totalInfluence}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, define its average
influence to be its total influence divided by $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Average coordinate flip probability]
\lean{FABL.averageCoordinateFlipProbability}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p003-b003,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p064-b009,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b002
}
\label{FABL.averageCoordinateFlipProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.uniformProbability}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its average coordinate flip
probability is the probability that $f(x)$ changes when a uniformly chosen coordinate of
a uniformly chosen input $x$ is flipped.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A power inequality for bounded exponents]
\lean{FABL.natCast_mul_one_sub_pow_le}
\label{FABL.natCast_mul_one_sub_pow_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $a\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0\le a\le1$, and let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $k\le n$.
Then $k(1-a^n)\le n(1-a^k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for an inverse-dimension power]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_inverse_dimension_pow_upper}
\label{FABL.one_sub_inverse_dimension_pow_upper}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For a positive integer $n$ and any natural number $k$, $1-(1-2/n)^k\le 2k/n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for an inverse-dimension power]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_inverse_dimension_pow_lower}
\label{FABL.one_sub_inverse_dimension_pow_lower}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.natCast_mul_one_sub_pow_le, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_pow_le_exp_neg_two}
\difficulty{5}
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $0<n$ and $k\le n$, \[ (1-\exp(-2))\frac{k}{n} \le
1-\left(1-\frac{2}{n}\right)^k, \] where the fractions are viewed as real numbers.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional
sign cube to $\{-1,1\}$. Its average influence, multiplied by $(1-e^{-2})/2$, is at most
its noise sensitivity at flip probability $1/n$, where the input is uniform and each
coordinate is independently flipped with that probability.
\end{theorem}
